method.filtering_summary: Live search at about 7:35 AM EAT on 16 sources pulled 2,536 postings (13 answered; Jobicy timed out, ReliefWeb failed again, and Wellfound's automated fetch is switched off so it was checked in Ben's signed-in browser instead). 1,706 were older than 7 days and 51 were old reposts, 210 senior or excluded titles, 177 not target roles, 182 excluded Kenya, 14 already applied and 67 duplicates, leaving 129. Roles already shown in earlier briefings were skipped. Jobgether answered live (495 offers, 199 from the last 7 days, 25 kept by the script), but every new engineering offer on close review was limited to one European country or asked 3+ years, so none made the list. micro1 answered live (59 pulled, 10 kept by the script); only one new role fits, Data Analyst (AI Evaluation), and it is at the top. Wellfound: about 45 listings reviewed in the signed-in browser, none fit (one vague US-time-zone listing, unpaid internships, static-site freelance work). Himalayas leads were confirmed through the Himalayas API and, for Canonical, the Greenhouse board.

stories.title: Musk confirms Grok Bot usage limits were tightened over cost
stories.summary: Some users saw weekly usage jump from as low as 50% to 100% over Halloween weekend; Musk wrote that "the cost of serving Grok Bot was unsustainably high relative to revenue" and has not said how limits will work going forward.
stories.why: Agent tools are getting pricier and more rationed, so knowing how to work efficiently within usage limits is becoming a real skill for AI engineers.

stories.title: Anthropic launches message threads beta for Claude API agents
stories.summary: Agents send the full conversation once, then only new messages plus the last reply ID; Anthropic says wait time on 500,000 to 1M token requests fell about 35%, with prices and rate limits unchanged and threads expiring five minutes after the last request.
stories.why: A practical API change for anyone building long-running coding or support agents, the kind of work Ben pitches in AI engineer applications.

stories.title: Deep Principle releases Hydrogen-1.0, a 753B open-weight science model
stories.summary: MIT-licensed post-train of Z.ai's GLM-5.3 with 1M-token context; self-reported 38.3% on FrontierScience-Research vs 33.3% for GPT-6-Astra; tested on 8 GPUs with SGLang behind an OpenAI-compatible API.
stories.why: Shows open weights moving into specialist domains, and the SGLang and quantized (NVFP4/MXFP4) serving setup lines up with Ben's vLLM and quantization experience.

stories.title: Trajectory raises $45M Series A for continual-learning post-training
stories.summary: The 18-person startup raised $45 million at a $300 million valuation, led by Sequoia with Nvidia, Bessemer and Bain Capital Ventures; customers include Harvey, Rogo, Decagon, Mercor and Nvidia, and its platform is now publicly available.
stories.why: Post-training open models from feedback is close to Ben's LoRA fine-tuning work, and a freshly funded small team is likely to be hiring.

stories.title: OPay shelves its $304 million US IPO a day after pricing
stories.summary: OPay priced its ADS at $19 but trading never started; it withdrew the NYSE listing, citing a regulatory inquiry in an undisclosed foreign jurisdiction, leaving a planned $4 billion valuation in limbo.
stories.why: A big signal on how hard it is for African fintechs to reach public markets, which shapes funding and hiring across the sector Ben works in.

stories.title: Nairobi took 41% of African tech funding in the first nine months of 2026
stories.summary: Tracxn says African tech raised $684 million in 9M 2026, up 30% from $527 million; Nairobi raised $277 million (41% of all funding), with Spiro the largest contributor; no new African unicorns this year.
stories.why: More capital landing in Nairobi means more local startups with money to hire engineers, though much of it sits with one company.

stories.title: Squarespace cuts 19% of staff, mostly product and engineering
stories.summary: About 300 jobs go; the CEO memo cites "smaller teams, more player coaches" and offers at least 16 weeks of base salary plus benefits through May 2027, as vibe-coding site builders reshape the market.
stories.why: Another sign that AI is shrinking traditional web engineering teams, so Ben's AI and agent skills matter more than plain front-end work.

stories.title: SUSE to cut about 10% of its workforce, citing automation and AI
stories.summary: The CEO memo to SUSE's 1,900 staff says "automation and AI are fundamentally shifting how software companies operate"; affected staff will be told by November 4.
stories.why: Open-source infrastructure companies are also trimming roles AI can cover, which means more competition for remote jobs from experienced engineers.

stories.title: Airtel Kenya buys 100MHz of 5G spectrum for KES 8.4 billion
stories.summary: Airtel got 25-year rights to 100MHz in the 3,500MHz band (about US$65 million); Kenya's 5G subscriptions reached 2.1 million in June 2026, up 75% from 1.2 million a year earlier.
stories.why: Stronger competition with Safaricom on data could mean cheaper, faster connectivity for the mobile products Kenyan developers build.

stories.title: KRA chair defends a 25% phone tax at network activation, though it is not law
stories.summary: The 25% activation tax was dropped from the Finance Act 2026, so the existing 10% excise duty on phones stays; KRA's chair argued import checks are beaten by under-declaration in consolidated cargo.
stories.why: Phone prices drive mobile and M-PESA adoption in Kenya, and the idea raises IMEI privacy questions relevant to anyone building local fintech.

stories.title: Kenswitch partners with PayU's Wibmo on 3-D Secure online card checks
stories.summary: Banks connected to Kenya's domestic payment switch get an EMV 3-D Secure Access Control Server, with risk-based checks using OTPs, biometrics or push approvals, plus stronger domestic e-commerce processing.
stories.why: Better local card authentication makes it easier for Kenyan web apps to take online card payments alongside M-PESA.
